title: controlled experiments
question: What is the main purpose of a control group?
lesson: A control group provides a baseline. Holding other conditions comparable helps isolate the effect of the tested intervention.

title: DNA information
question: Which molecule carries hereditary sequence information in most cellular life?
lesson: DNA stores hereditary information in its nucleotide sequence. Cells transcribe parts of that information into RNA.

title: natural selection
question: Natural selection requires heritable variation and what else?
lesson: If heritable variants differ in survival or reproduction, their frequencies can change across generations.

title: replication
question: Why replicate an experiment?
lesson: Replication estimates variability and tests whether a result is reproducible rather than an accident of one sample.

title: derivative
question: What is d(x²)/dx?
lesson: The power rule gives d(x^n)/dx = n x^(n-1). Therefore d(x²)/dx = 2x.

title: Bayes rule
question: Which expression equals P(A|B) when P(B)>0?
lesson: Bayes' rule follows from conditional probability: P(A|B)=P(B|A)P(A)/P(B).

title: matrix dimensions
question: An m×n matrix times an n×p matrix has which shape?
lesson: The inner dimensions contract; the remaining outer dimensions are m and p.

title: prime numbers
question: Which is a prime number?
lesson: A prime integer greater than one has exactly two positive divisors: one and itself.

title: reinforcement learning
question: What signal directly defines the objective in standard RL?
lesson: An RL agent selects actions to maximize expected cumulative reward. Reward is distinct from observations and actions.

title: overfitting
question: What best detects overfitting?
lesson: A widening gap between training and held-out performance indicates that a model may be fitting training-specific details.

title: supervised learning
question: Supervised learning trains primarily from what?
lesson: Supervised learning uses examples paired with target labels or values to learn a predictive mapping.

title: attention
question: In scaled dot-product attention, what is softmax applied to?
lesson: Attention forms query-key scores, scales them, applies softmax, then uses the weights to combine values.

title: Newton's second law
question: For constant mass, which equation states Newton's second law?
lesson: Net force equals mass times acceleration: F = ma.

title: photon energy
question: How is photon energy related to frequency?
lesson: Planck's relation is E = hν, so photon energy is proportional to frequency.

title: vacuum light speed
question: Approximately how fast does light travel in vacuum?
lesson: The defined SI value is 299,792,458 metres per second, approximately 3×10⁸ m/s.

title: entropy
question: For an isolated system, the second law says total entropy does what?
lesson: The entropy of an isolated system does not decrease; irreversible processes typically increase it.

title: modus ponens
question: If P implies Q, and P is true, what follows?
lesson: Modus ponens is the valid form: P→Q; P; therefore Q.

title: Cogito attribution
question: Who is most associated with 'I think, therefore I am'?
lesson: The formulation is associated with René Descartes and his method of radical doubt.

title: falsifiability
question: In Popper's account, a scientific theory should be open to what?
lesson: Popper emphasized falsifiability: a scientific claim should risk conflict with possible observations.
source: Karl Popper, The Logic of Scientific Discovery

title: simulation inference
question: Saying 'I am simulated' proves consciousness: true or false?
lesson: False. A sentence can be generated by rules or training. It is behavioral evidence requiring interpretation, not proof of subjective experience.

title: dramatic irony
question: What is dramatic irony?
lesson: Dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows consequential information that one or more characters do not.
options: The audience knows more than a character

title: unreliable narrator
question: What makes a narrator unreliable?
lesson: An unreliable narrator's account gives readers reason to doubt its accuracy or completeness because of bias, limitation, or deception.

title: blank verse
question: What is blank verse in English poetry?
lesson: Blank verse is unrhymed verse, conventionally written in iambic pentameter.
source: The Princeton Encyclopedia of Poetry and Poetics

title: metaphor
question: What does a metaphor do?
lesson: A metaphor describes one thing in terms of another without requiring a literal identity, creating a conceptual comparison.
